source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (Macedonian e-Commerce Association)
why_relevant: Merchant-side association for online commerce; publishes quarterly analyses of online transaction value/volume built on NBRSM data, signed an MoU with the Ministry of Digital Transformation, and lobbies on cashless payments within the 'Smart MK 2030' agenda. Bridges merchant interests and payments policy.

Second-largest chamber (Albanian-language business community, active since 2005, contact info@oemvp.org). Runs parallel consultations and position statements; important for language coverage (sq) and for SME/merchant reactions that the Skopje chamber does not capture. URL inferred from the published contact domain — treat as unverified.

source_name: Сојуз на стопански комори на Македонија (Union of Chambers of Commerce)
why_relevant: Umbrella of ~35 chambers and 30+ associations, including the Chamber of Accountants, Financiers and Tax Advisors. Aggregates business-side reactions to fiscal and financial draft laws and reveals additional sub-chambers relevant to payments. Homepage URL inferred from its Facebook handle (www.chamber.mk) — unverified.

Publishes explicit advocacy positions on financial regulation — e.g. an item endorsing amendments to the AML/CFT regulation to harmonise with EU rules. Its committees produce written comments on draft laws affecting banks and payment firms, in English (useful cross-check on mk-only drafts).

130+ members from 20 countries spanning banking, insurance, consulting and audit; its stated purpose is concrete reform proposals to Macedonian authorities. FIC white-book style recommendations name contested provisions and implementation deadlines. Site uses legacy ASPX query-string routing.

source_name: biznisregulativa.mk — chamber/association registry entry (MASIT and others)
why_relevant: A government-side business-regulation portal that lists recognised chambers ('Komoris') — useful as an authoritative index for enumerating which chambers/associations formally exist and are consulted, rather than relying on search discovery.

source_name: ФУЛМ Штедилница — republication of MBA announcements
why_relevant: Member institutions republish MBA соопштенија verbatim. Member sites act as a mirror when the association's own posting is delayed or removed, and reveal which announcements members choose to amplify.

The chamber serves raw PDFs from a flat upload path — search surfaced both annual activity reports and a 'Предлог на закон за изменување и дополнување на Законот за банките' PDF hosted there. This is where the actual draft-law texts and chamber commentary attachments live.

source_name: Ekonomija i biznis (Економија и Бизнис) — magazine and portal
why_relevant: Long-running monthly business magazine with an online edition; publishes analytical/expert commentary and interviews (including with central bank governors at its conferences) rather than wire copy. Useful for regulatory intent and expert reading of new banking/payments law, not just events.

source_name: MIA — Media Information Agency (Медиумска информативна агенција)
why_relevant: State news agency; carries governor/deputy-governor statements, IMF Article IV and FSAP-type conclusions on NBRM, and official announcements verbatim. Its wire copy is republished across MK outlets, so it is an upstream node for most regulatory news.

Major daily with an active economy desk that covers banking fees, consumer-facing payment rules, parliamentary passage of financial laws and interviews with officials. Named in the cell definition; included on outlet knowledge rather than a confirmed article hit in this run.

Investigative outlet historically covering bank failures, licence revocations and supervisory controversy (the type of reporting that surfaces enforcement before formal publication). Named in the cell definition; not confirmed by an article hit in this run.
Business/economy news portal covering company and financial-sector news; useful as a redundancy channel and for picking up NBRM and Ministry of Finance announcements that larger outlets skip.

Aggregates virtually all MK-language outlets into one searchable, clustered stream. The single most efficient discovery layer for this cell: one keyword sweep surfaces which outlet broke a supervisory story and reveals smaller portals not otherwise on the map. Also preserves items after publisher URLs rot.

Consumer/tech portal that reported the switch away from SMS OTP to a stricter security regime for online card payments in North Macedonia — i.e. it renders operational payment-rule change dates in plain language, which formal NBRM documents state only obliquely. Useful for SCA/3DS-type deadline signals.

Business information/database service with news layer; potentially useful for company-level context around licensed payment institutions and financial companies mentioned in regulatory news. Lower priority — commercial database rather than a regulatory news desk.

Kapital's longer-form management/market analysis arm; carries structural pieces on the banking market (ownership, who-is-who, market shares) that give the actor map behind supervisory news. Tracked separately from the main portal because it has its own URL space and cadence.

Daily with an economy desk that covers banking and finance; candidate redundancy channel for supervisory news. Included from outlet knowledge and cell scope; not confirmed by an article hit in this run — verify before promoting.

Metamorphosis Foundation's news agency; covers digital policy, consumer rights and institutional transparency, which intersects with payments regulation and data/consumer-protection obligations on banks. Candidate; not confirmed by an article hit in this run.
